text.text: A record of what you own and owe, nothing more. Update balances monthly, add a snapshot, and watch the line move. This is a tracking sheet and gives no advice.
Accounts
Holdings
Snapshots
Ten-minute routine
Update the balance on every account
Update current value on each holding
Add a snapshot for each account
Check that liabilities went down as expected
Keep values in one currency per account. Use the Currency column to mark any that differ.
Keeping the history honest

A snapshot is a dated photograph of a balance. Never edit an old one to match a later correction; add a new snapshot with the correct figure and a note. The history is only useful if it shows what you believed on each date.
Net worth is the total of your assets minus the total of your liabilities. Class says which is which; liabilities are stored as positive amounts.
Reading the columns
Counts toward net worth shows an asset as a plus and a liability as a minus, so adding the column up gives the figure.
Balance not itemised is what is left in an account after its listed holdings.
Highest, lowest and last reading come from the snapshots linked to the account.
